showcase_raglibrary_desc: Semantic search over any document — plus a library of ready-made buckets: RAG, Skills, and community-published MCP connectors.
showcase_planremember_desc: Complex tasks broken down automatically, step by step in real time — and Remember learns from your sessions, creating and updating skills on its own.

capabilities_subtitle: Every capability below is shared between you and the agent — not hidden behind a tool call.
capability_browser_desc: Real DevTools — console, network, a visual panel — plus Playwright and auto-detected dev servers. You and the agent see the same page.
capability_sandbox_desc: Native isolation on every platform: bubblewrap + seccomp + Landlock on Linux, WSL2 on Windows, Seatbelt on macOS — not a generic Docker container.
capability_context_graph_desc: A typed code graph across ~30 languages (tree-sitter), impact analysis, and GraphRAG — the same source of truth the agent's tool and your UI both query.
capability_terminal_desc: A persistent PTY session — survives navigation and remounts, the same shell seen live by you and the agent, inside the sandbox, when active.
capability_git_desc: Isolated worktrees, stash, diff/merge in an overlay, and PR creation without leaving the app.
capability_explorer_desc: Optimistic conflict resolution when you and the agent edit the same file, full-text search shared with the agent's own tool, and per-commit file history.
why_privacy_desc: No conversation, document or code is sent to third parties. LGPD, GDPR and internal policy compliance.
why_cost_desc: Fixed price for the Vectora license. LLM costs under your control — use local models for free.
why_custom_desc: Configure LLM providers, embedding models, chunk size, system prompts and much more.
why_sovereign_desc: No lock-in. No cloud dependency. Run offline if needed. Your server, your rules.

faq_geral_1_answer: Vectora is a self-hosted AI agent with RAG, a native Context Graph, and multi-user web chat — it runs on your own computer or server, never in a Vectora cloud.
faq_geral_2_answer: You download and install Vectora (Windows, macOS, or Linux) — it's a native app, not a Docker image. Teams that need shared web chat usually run the Linux build on their own VPS; Docker is only used to spin up the optional infrastructure for 'complete' storage mode (Postgres+Qdrant+Redis), never for Vectora itself.
faq_geral_3_question: Do I need a GPU to run it?
faq_geral_3_answer: No. Vectora uses LLMs and embeddings via API (Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage, OpenRouter) or local Ollama. For individual use, any recent laptop runs it fine; for a team VPS, 2 vCPUs and 4 GB RAM are already enough.
faq_instalacao_1_answer: Windows 10+, macOS 12+, and Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 11+/Fedora 35+) — native installers for all three, with built-in auto-update.
faq_instalacao_2_question: How do I deploy on a server for my team?
faq_instalacao_2_answer: Any Linux VPS with 2+ vCPUs and 4+ GB RAM — AWS, GCP, Hetzner, DigitalOcean, or your provider of choice. It's the same Linux installer (.AppImage/.deb/.rpm), just running on a server instead of your desktop.
faq_instalacao_3_answer: Less than 5 minutes: download the installer for your system, open the app, and create your root account on first launch. 'Complete' storage mode (optional, for scaling beyond the default SQLite+LanceDB) is deployed via a separate docker-compose — that part does take a few extra minutes.
faq_planos_1_question: What's the difference between Free and Pro?
faq_planos_1_answer: Free is free forever and requires no account: operational CLI, Desktop, and unlimited RAG (via Cohere/Voyage/Ollama), all running on your machine. Pro (R$24/month) requires an account and adds what only makes sense for teams: multi-user web chat, unlimited member invites, SSO/SAML, scalable storage (Postgres/Qdrant/Redis), webhooks, and priority support.
faq_planos_2_question: Do I need to create an account to use Vectora?
faq_planos_2_answer: No, not for local/solo use. The Free plan works 100% without login. An account is only needed for Pro's team features.
faq_planos_3_answer: Yes. No minimum commitment. Cancel from the dashboard anytime — your account automatically reverts to the Free plan.
faq_seguranca_1_question: Is my data sent to Vectora?
faq_seguranca_1_answer: No. Everything stays on your server. Vectora has no access to your documents, conversations, or code.
faq_seguranca_2_question: Is Vectora LGPD and GDPR compliant?
faq_seguranca_2_answer: Yes. Since your data stays on your own infrastructure, you keep full control over compliance.
faq_seguranca_3_answer: On Free, it's local use with no login. For Pro (account required), Vectora's own authentication supports email/password and magic links.
faq_tecnico_1_answer: Google Gemini (default), Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama (local), OpenRouter (proxy with hundreds of models), and any OpenAI-API-compatible provider.
faq_tecnico_2_answer: Embeddings via Cohere, Voyage, Ollama, or OpenRouter (local or hosted), LanceDB as the default vector store with dense vector search and optional reranking (Cohere/Voyage). In Complete mode (self-hosted with Postgres + Qdrant), search becomes hybrid (dense + BM25).
faq_tecnico_3_question: Does Vectora expose a public API or MCP server?
faq_tecnico_3_answer: No. Vectora is a workspace with AI — you and the agent share the filesystem, terminal, git, and browser inside the product itself, with no public REST API or embedded MCP server.

downloads_install_windows: Run the .exe and follow the installer. If Windows SmartScreen warns you, click "More info" → "Run anyway" (common for new apps until the certificate builds reputation). Prefer silent install? Use Vectora-Setup.exe /S. The .msi integrates with Apps & Features — useful for IT-managed rollouts.
downloads_install_macos: Drag Vectora.app into the Applications folder. If Gatekeeper blocks it from opening, run xattr -cr /Applications/Vectora.app once in Terminal.
downloads_install_linux: AppImage: chmod +x Vectora-*.AppImage && ./Vectora-*.AppImage. Or install the native package: sudo dpkg -i vectora_*.deb (Debian/Ubuntu) or sudo rpm -i vectora-*.rpm (Fedora/RHEL).
